Name: Flare
Distinguishing Features: Glowing streaks going up neck and spine
History: The recent law passed in Florida about state-sanctioned kidnapping of mutant minors was controversial but seemingly theoretical. When a high-school basketball game was interrupted by one of the cheering students seemingly erupting in light & knocking out the power for three blocks, an investigation occurred, and state officials came to the home of Taylor Crenshaw and her parents begrudgingly handed her over despite protests. It garnered national media coverage.
Personality: Energetic, impatient, tactless. Very ADHD, very inexperienced.
Goal: Taylor sees her power as something to be celebrated, not hidden, and wants to do good with it.
Barrier: Taylor knows that being able to remain with her family and friends means pretending that she isn’t a mutant.

Name: Half-Life
History: Cody went to jail for assaulting a school resource officer during an altercation at his high school in Atlanta.
Was tried and convicted as an adult. Currently in violation of parole.
He has managed to avoid getting outed as a mutant so far.
Personality: Aggressive, unfocused, impulsive, resentful of the state.
Goal: Is seeking to shake off the restrictions and constraints that has hampered him.
Barrier: Cody is in denial that mere “freedom from” is sufficient. His goal is purely reductive right now, but he lacks a positive vision of the future, for himself or for others.

Name: Regret
History: Left home in Houston before he could be kicked out. He feels deeply conflicted about his power, as he deems it coercive. He left home out of fear that he couldn’t trust his parents’ acceptance of him. They still don’t know he’s a mutant.
Been with X-FRONT less than a year. Has been supportive of Toya's leadership, and was involved in the rescue operation for Hermes.
Personality: Deeply emotionally intelligent, balanced between emotion and intellect. He’s soft-spoken, but speaks and acts decisively.
Goal: Mohamed has hope for a world of mutant-human acceptance. He sees the direct action of X-FRONT as a temporary necessity, and looks forward to the day that it can be disbanded.
Barrier: The present is not that time. X-FRONT is very necessary to correct the absurd injustices that cannot wait for resolution.

Entries.name: Telepathic Link
Entries.text: The character can communicate telepathically with one person at a time, and they must have met or seen the other person before. The communication can be verbal, visual or even more complex, such as imparting location information. There is no limit to the distance of the communication, as long as the character and the target are in the same dimension. If the other person does not wish to speak with the character, the target can automatically tune them out. To force a telepathic link, the character can make a Logic check against the target’s Vigilance defense. On a failure, the character cannot attempt to communicate with the target in this way for the rest of the day. On a success, the character can communicate with the target for as long as the concentration lasts. On a Fantastic success, the target cannot shut the character out for the rest of the day.

Name: Stasis
History: Grew up in an evangelical Latino family in Arizona. When his X-gene expressed itself at 13, his family's pastor at River of God Church tried to pray it away, and when that didn't work, recommended the Sanctuary Hills Youth Reformation Campus in the desert. Hermes' parents voluntarily sent him.
He escaped the mutant conversion therapy camp with the assistance of X-FRONT four months prior.
Personality: Hermes wakes up in the night terrified that he’s going to be kidnapped again.
Goal: Moving past the trauma, and allowing that horribly experience to energize action, rather than paralyze.
Barrier: The feelings of loss are overwhelming. There is unprocessed grief and anger that cannot be accessed because the panic is overwhelming. Hard to appreciate what he does have.

Sections.Heading: Elemental Control: Velocity
Description: With a touch, he can paralyze anyone or anything; another touch he can release them. They are conscious throughout but trapped in an unmoving body. The body can be moved by external forces, just not of its own volition.

Name: Taboo
History: They briefly attended Xavier’s academy and felt that it was cowardly at best. After repeated arguments and conflicts with the teachers, they dropped out.
Met Toya at a mutant pride march that went south, and formed the seeds of X-FRONT together.
Personality: Goal: Tabitha doesn’t see a future for herself worth having, except if it’s a means to the end of other mutants also having a future. She’s going to fight hard and go down fighting.

Barrier: Tabitha has broken off from those she felt limited her, but that also deprives her of institutional and social support. The future she wants to build, she can’t build alone, but she almost compulsively burns every bridge she crosses.

Name: Tank
History: Had attended the mutant pride march in Tallahassee, tried to go incognito, but when things started getting rough they stepped up to protect the marchers when the police wouldn’t.
Having faced the seeming failure of protesting and petitioning, Toya has used that rejection to energize their commitment to direct action, having formed X-FRONT with Tabitha.
Personality: As the eldest and co-founder of X-Front, Toya has a presumption to authority and resists accountability.
Goal: They want the freedom to act with the power of the group behind them, but chafe at being told what to do.

Barrier: Given the volatile combination of the members of X-FRONT leadership requires self-control, confidence, and clarity. Ambiguity and recklessness lead to pulling in different directions, impeding progress, and frustrations.

Entries.text: The character makes a ranged attack with an edge at an enemy in line of sight. For this attack, add +1 to the character’s Agility damage bonus for every 2 points of Focus they spend. Entries.name: Elemental Barrier
Entries.text: The character forms a wall of their element within their line of sight and up to 10 spaces away per rank. This covers up to 2 spaces across (vertically/horizontally) per their rank. The character makes an Agility check and compares the results against the Agility defense of any target in the affected spaces. On a success, the character chooses which side of the barrier the target winds up on. On a failure, the target chooses. On a Fantastic success, the target has trouble on all actions for one round. Attacks against the barrier are against the character’s Ego defense. Any attacks against it that do 10 points of damage or less are instantly absorbed, and the barrier continues. If an attack does more than 10 points of damage, it destroys the barrier. Either way, the attack leaves those behind the barrier unharmed.

Entries.name: Elemental Sphere
Entries.group: Standard or Reaction, Concentration, Cost: 5 Focus
Entries.text: The character envelops themselves—and any chosen people within up to 5 spaces times their rank—in a protective sphere comprised of their element. When the sphere is formed, the character makes an Ego check and compares the results against the Agility defense of unwanted characters in the enclosed spaces. On a success, the character can move any unwanted people within the sphere’s perimeter to spaces outside of the sphere. On a Fantastic success, such moved people suffer full damage and have trouble on all actions for one round. Attacks against the sphere are against the character’s Ego defense. Any attacks against the sphere are absorbed as if made against the character’s Elemental Protection power, and the sphere continues. If an attack does more damage than the character’s Elemental Protection power can sustain, it destroys the sphere, but no one inside is harmed.
